title.text: Wet-road traction and changing traffic speeds

why_how.text: Hydroplaning occurs when tires begin riding on water instead of maintaining road contact; slowing in rain or on a wet road helps prevent it. The phrase “when” limits how this instruction applies. Keep that condition with the stated action rather than broadening the rule.

Bald or badly worn tires can lose wet-road traction at lower speeds. Keep the described person, vehicle and situation attached to the instruction. A similar topic does not make different conditions interchangeable.

If the tires seem to lose road grip, ease pressure off the accelerator. Keep the described person, vehicle and situation attached to the instruction. A similar topic does not make different conditions interchangeable.

When grip is lost, keep the wheel straight and avoid stopping or turning until traction returns; if an emergency demands a turn, make it slowly. The phrase “When” limits how this instruction applies. Keep that condition with the stated action rather than broadening the rule.

Repeatedly driving faster than traffic and passing creates additional collision opportunities. Keep the described person, vehicle and situation attached to the instruction. A similar topic does not make different conditions interchangeable.

If traffic collects behind a much slower vehicle, its driver should pull aside when safe and let others pass. The phrase “when” limits how this instruction applies. Keep that condition with the stated action rather than broadening the rule.
Use an entrance ramp to build toward traffic speed before merging. The phrase “before” limits how this instruction applies. Keep that condition with the stated action rather than broadening the rule.

Avoid reaching the end of an entrance ramp and stopping; if waiting for a gap, slow earlier so room remains to accelerate. Keep the described person, vehicle and situation attached to the instruction. A similar topic does not make different conditions interchangeable.

For an exit ramp, remain with traffic speed on the main road and slow after moving onto the ramp. The phrase “after” limits how this instruction applies. Keep that condition with the stated action rather than broadening the rule.

When turning from a high-speed two-lane road with traffic behind, signal and use brake lights before reducing speed quickly but safely. The phrase “When” limits how this instruction applies. Keep that condition with the stated action rather than broadening the rule.

Identify slow vehicles early so a lane change or speed reduction can be made gradually. Keep the described person, vehicle and situation attached to the instruction. A similar topic does not make different conditions interchangeable.
